published_on: site/flagged.html (appended after v2's register and v6's findings)

flags.what_is_wrong: The 2026-11-19 official injury report was not read in this session, so the availability column on the slate has nothing to put in it. An availability number invented from a stale report would be worse than no number, because the whole point of the column is that it is current.
flags.what_is_published: Every slate row prints the column as a blank with F-V7-AVAIL as the reason, and gate G-V7-8 fails while it is blank. Rotation-availability strategies are therefore blocked rather than quietly dropped.

flags.what_is_wrong: The league's own pages disagree by one date: the three team-stat pages run through 2026-11-17, while /standings includes 2026-11-18. Measured on Utah, whose stat-page games played (15) is one short of its standings record (3-13 = 16), the extra game being the 11/18 win over the Lakers.
flags.what_is_published: Both clocks are published side by side with the size of the gap, instead of being blended into a single as-of date that is true of neither page.

flags.what_is_wrong: The transcription cannot be reproduced from this sandbox — nba.com resets the TLS handshake (curl exit 000), so no number could be re-read by script — and it cannot be reproduced from a GitHub runner either, where stats.nba.com times out and cdn.nba.com returns 403.
flags.what_is_published: The numbers were read page by page and committed to nba2/v7/official.py, and three arithmetic identities are tested over all 30 clubs so a transcription slip fails the build instead of reaching a reader: NetRtg = OffRtg − DefRtg (30/30), PTS − OppPTS = +/− (30/30), and every club's W equals its wins in the committed finals (30/30 over 222 games).

flags.what_is_wrong: No market price exists anywhere in this repository — no closing line, no opening line, no spread or total quote — so no edge is computable and the blend weight against the closing line is undefined.
flags.what_is_published: Every stake on the slate is 0.00. Gate G-V7-6 blocks every price-dependent strategy. The strategies are written and published in the blocked state rather than deleted, so the gate's arithmetic is visible.

flags.what_is_wrong: Player props cannot be priced: the largest committed per-player log set holds 3 games for the best-covered player (421 players, max 3 games each), while a ±5-point line needs about 15 games before a residual standard deviation means anything.
flags.what_is_published: The props section prints the arithmetic — the sample it has against the sample it needs — instead of a probability. Player-prop combos are blocked on that basis.

flags.what_is_wrong: The snapshot this layer is cut from is dated 2026-11-19T06:05Z and the official pages have since moved: an independent re-read on 2026-11-19 measures LAL at GP 16 (13-3) and NOP at 16 GP, where this snapshot holds LAL 15 GP (13-2) and NOP 15 GP (5-11). Two clubs are one game further on than the inputs on this page.
flags.what_is_published: The inputs are not silently re-cut. The slate, the ratings and every derived number stay pinned to the stamped snapshot, the later reading is published here rather than being counted as a match, and a re-cut is a new snapshot with a new retrieval stamp. A reader pricing Friday's games should prefer the newer official page for those two clubs.

flags.what_is_wrong: Pre-registration hashes are committed in the same commit as the strategy definitions they freeze. That makes them tamper-evident against later edits, but not against a rewrite of the commit that introduced both — a hash stored beside its own input proves only ordering, not authorship.
flags.what_is_published: Ten pre-registration files are written and the build refuses to overwrite an existing one, so any change to a strategy's signal, thresholds, universe or settlement rule after freezing fails the build. The stronger fix is a suggestion, not a silent claim.

flags.what_is_wrong: GitHub Pages is configured with build_type: legacy, source branch main, path /. Under legacy mode the uploaded site/ artefact is not what gets served from the root, and a push alone does not trigger a redeploy — the deploy must be dispatched explicitly.
flags.what_is_published: The workflow now dispatches pages.yml explicitly, and this session re-dispatched and then re-read the live page to confirm the deployment landed rather than assuming the push was enough.

flags.what_is_wrong: The first draft of the v7 model cut its team ratings from the 2026-11-19 pages and then used those same ratings to 'test' October games — a leak of future information into every historical prediction.
flags.what_is_published: Fixed before publication. The measured symptom was a 34.1% walk-forward accuracy, which is the signature of a sign or leak bug rather than a bad model; the fix restricts every historical cut to ratings_as_of(cutoff), and a test now fails if a future rating is used. Corrected walk-forward: 67.1% accuracy, log-loss 0.6349.

flags.what_is_wrong: The v3/v4/v5 trees are measurably stale on the inputs that matter: v3 prices Atlanta at 8-6 while the live standings page prints 9-6, and no tree in the repository contained the twelve 2026-11-18 finals. They were not edited in place — that is another session's scope — a new layer was cut instead.
flags.what_is_published: The v7 slate is cut entirely from the 2026-11-19 snapshot and reconciles 30/30 against the committed finals. The older surfaces keep their published numbers and their own as-of dates, and the discrepancy is stated here rather than quietly patched.
